Basic Information

  • Full Project Title: Irradiation-Damage-Resistant Refractory High-Entropy Alloys for Advanced Modular Reactors
  • Host Institution: University of Birmingham
  • Department: School of Metallurgy and Materials
  • Supervisor: Prof. Sandy Knowles
  • Industry Partner: UK National Nuclear Laboratory (UKNNL)
  • Study Level: PhD / EngD
  • Duration: 4 years
  • Start Date: 2026 cohort
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded (UK students)
  • Stipend: £26,805 per year (tax-free, enhanced rate)
  • Tuition Fees: Covered
  • Eligibility: UK students
  • Application Deadline: 6 November 2026
  • Programme: PANDA DFA training programme included

Project Description

This 4-year PhD/EngD project aims to design refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) resistant to irradiation damage for advanced modular nuclear reactors (AMRs). The research will involve computational design of new alloys, production via arc melting or additive manufacturing, and characterisation using advanced electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction techniques. The project includes the PANDA DFA training programme.

About University of Birmingham

The University of Birmingham is a public research university in Birmingham, England, and a Russell Group member. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral study across engineering, medicine, science, business, humanities and social sciences. Research and teaching bring together different disciplines to investigate challenges affecting health, technology, communities and the environment.

Official website: https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/
